writeup.headline: IMAX rates Buy on solid growth, strong margins and momentum, sitting just at the Hold edge.
writeup.thesis: IMAX scores 65, exactly at the Buy threshold, so the rating rests on a thin margin. Strength comes from trend (81), with shares up 74.8% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago and 26.6 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days, and from the balance sheet (78), with net debt at 0.66 times free cash flow. Growth (71) reflects TTM revenue growth of 14.8% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 12.2% year on year, and quality (71) is backed by a 20.2% operating margin and a 30.4% FCF margin. Valuation (46) holds the score back: a P/S of 6.7x and EV/EBIT of 34.0x are high in absolute terms, the FCF yield is 0.4 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, and against its own history the stock is near the middle of its own history (the multiples disagree: P/S expensive, P/FCF cheap, EV/EBIT middle). News risk (49) is roughly neutral: broker target raises are offset by Disney's competing Infinity Vision large-format push.
key_risks: Competition from Disney's Infinity Vision large-format label, which spans roughly three times as many screens as IMAX
Results depend on the film slate, and the Q3 2026 report on Nov 5 could disappoint after the strong run
Valuation is high in absolute terms (P/S 6.7x, EV/EBIT 34.0x), and P/S is more expensive than at 58 of the last 61 month-ends
Diluted share count up 2.5% year on year, with stock-based compensation at 6.5% of revenue
Price 3.9% below its 50-day average and 10.3% below its 52-week high, signs that momentum may be cooling
what_would_change: A drop of just 1 point in the composite score would move the rating to Hold, for example from weaker trend or news risk after the Nov 5 results
Escalation of the Disney Infinity Vision threat or a guidance cut would pull news risk down and likely tip the rating to Hold
Reaching Strong Buy needs 15 more points, which would take sustained growth acceleration plus a cheaper valuation or more positive news
